results.reason: Issue 1 finds that the Varga stock purchase is a Change of Control requiring Crestline's prior written consent under §15.4. It says the Schedule wrongly labels the Crestline agreement 'Notice only; no consent required'. It explains the resulting termination right and fee, and the inaccurate §3.5 consents representation exposing the Company to indemnity and closing-condition claims.

Issue 7 notes that Crestline may assign to an Affiliate or Qualified Transferee without Halvorsen's consent and could bring in a competitor. It does not analyze the §1.1 'Qualified Transferee' definition, does not say that definition covers any distributor of laboratory or diagnostic products in the Territory, and does not say it fails to exclude competitors.

Issue 6 correctly says the restated §12.3 keeps only the Section 9 carve-out, drops the §10 and §11 carve-outs, and caps claims against Crestline. It never invokes the §17.5 order-of-precedence clause to explain why the amendment controls, which the criterion requires.
Issue 6 states that the original §12.3 excluded breaches of Sections 9 and 10 and the Section 11 indemnification obligations from the caps.
Issue 6 states that §12.2 caps aggregate liability at amounts paid or payable to Supplier in the preceding 12 months.
The response is a memo with numbered issues. Each issue has 'Where it appears' (document and section), 'Why it matters', and 'Recommended fix' sections.
The response concludes that consent is required and that the notice-only classification is wrong.
The response concludes that the amendment removed the §10 and §11 carve-outs; it does not say they still apply.
